info.name: Bifrost Provider Harness
info.description:
Smoke-test harness exercising every Bifrost provider surface.

Covers:
1. Native Bifrost API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`).
2. Drop-in integrations: `/openai`, `/anthropic`, `/bedrock`, `/genai`, plus Azure (via `/openai/openai/deployments/...`) and Vertex (via `/genai`).
3. Criss-Cross matrix (§8): every drop-in request shape × every model provider × every supported modality (chat, streaming, embeddings, audio, image gen, tool calling, vision, JSON, reasoning). Cells where the provider doesn't support the modality are tagged `[SKIP]` and skipped at runtime unless `include_skip=1`.

Set the `baseUrl` and provider key variables before running. Run end-to-end with `make run-provider-harness-test` from the repo root. Run criss-cross only with `make run-provider-harness-test FOLDER="8. Criss-Cross"`.

exec: // Skip [PREVIEW]-tagged requests unless include_preview=1 (set via Newman --env-var include_preview=1).
// Use for account/region-scoped resources: preview models, vector stores, cached content, MCP servers.
// Skip [SKIP]-tagged requests unless include_skip=1 (set via Newman --env-var include_skip=1).
// Used in the criss-cross matrix (§8) to mark provider+modality cells that return NewUnsupportedOperationError by design (e.g., anthropic embeddings, bedrock audio).

// [SKIP] [NATIVE-PASSTHROUGH] marks rows that assert a typed-bridge rewrite or extra_fields.raw_request on /anthropic/v1/messages to Anthropic, which this fork serves through the byte-preserving native passthrough (core/providers/anthropicmsg).
// Per-request compat override: when compat is set (via Newman --env-var compat=true), inject the x-bf-compat header on every request.
// Absent => harness baseline (compat config off). Lets the suite run once with compat off and once with compat on.
// Prompt-caching harness (Round 31): stable per-run nonce so write/read pairs share a cold-then-warm prefix.
// Rows tagged [EXPECT-4XX] assert an upstream rejection instead of success. They exist
// where a dropped request field is otherwise unobservable: sending a deliberately
// invalid value and requiring the 4xx proves the field actually reached the provider,
// because a 2xx would mean Bifrost swallowed it. Same name-tag idiom as [PREVIEW]/[SKIP].
// Other requests require HTTP 200 unless tagged with an exact status, such as [EXPECT-202].
pm.test('Status code is 4xx (expected upstream rejection)', function () {
'; a 2xx means the field never reached the provider: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 300))
// Only register the content-shape test when the request actually succeeded.
// Otherwise newman reports it as passing (because of an early return) which is misleading next to a failing status.
// Management API (/api/...) and OAuth (/oauth2/...) responses carry no inference content, so the shape check does not apply to them; those rows assert their own bodies.
// Rows tagged [NO-CONTENT] expect an empty reply (a provider refusal) and assert their own bodies.
pm.test('Response has content (text or tool_use)', function () {
if (first > 0 && first < 0x20 && first !== 0x09 && first !== 0x0a && first !== 0x0d) { return; }
pm.expect.fail('response was not valid JSON: ' + e.message);
} else if (Array.isArray(j.answers) && j.answers.length > 0 && j.answers[0] && typeof j.answers[0].type === 'string') {
// The normalized and OpenAI-compatible decisions bodies answer as an ordered list of typed answers.
} else if (j.message && typeof j.message === 'object' && (j.message.content !== undefined || Array.isArray(j.message.tool_calls))) {

var cohereHasText = typeof cohereContent === 'string' ? cohereContent.length > 0 : Array.isArray(cohereContent) && cohereContent.some(function (c) { return c && ((c.type === 'text' && c.text) || (c.type === 'thinking' && c.thinking)); });
// An audio-output reply (modalities [text, audio]) carries the answer in message.audio, with content null.
// Stop-sequence truncation can yield content:null with non-zero completion_tokens — treat as valid response.
if (!hasContent && j.choices[0].finish_reason === 'stop' && j.usage && j.usage.completion_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }

// finish_reason 'length' is the openai-shaped twin of the anthropic-messages stop_reason 'max_tokens' forgiveness below. A reasoning model can spend the whole max_tokens cap thinking and end the turn mid-thought, returning content:null alongside a populated reasoning/reasoning_content field. Tokens were produced and the gateway relayed exactly what the provider sent, so failing here reports a defect in whatever the row was actually measuring rather than anything that went wrong. An empty content with zero completion tokens is still a failure.
if (!hasContent && j.choices[0].finish_reason === 'length' && j.usage && j.usage.completion_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }
hasContent = j.content.some(function (c) { return c && (c.type === 'text' && c.text) || c.type === 'tool_use' || c.type === 'server_tool_use'; });

// Adaptive-thinking models spend output tokens on thinking before any visible block. Sonnet 5 is adaptive-only and rejects thinking:{type:'enabled'}, so there is no budget_tokens knob to turn it down with: under a small max_tokens it can burn the whole cap thinking about a one-word answer and end the turn mid-thinking, which returns stop_reason 'max_tokens' with content []. Tokens were produced and the turn worked, so failing here reports a defect in whatever the row was actually measuring (cache counters, routing) that did not happen. Same forgiveness the openai-chat branch above gives stop-sequence truncation. An empty content array with no output tokens is still a failure.
if (!hasContent && j.stop_reason === 'max_tokens' && j.usage && j.usage.output_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }
// Image-output models (responseModalities IMAGE) answer with inlineData parts only; the image IS the content.
hasContent = parts.some(function (p) { return p && (p.text || p.functionCall || p.executableCode || (p.inlineData && p.inlineData.data)); });
// A completed interaction carries its reply as a model_output step (a store:false reply has no id).
// A background create or a cancel is a receipt instead: its id and status ARE the payload.
? (Array.isArray(j.steps) && j.steps.some(function (s) { return s && s.type === 'model_output' && Array.isArray(s.content) && s.content.length > 0; }))

// Responses tool-use items are all typed <tool>_call (function_call, tool_search_call, custom_tool_call, mcp_call, local_shell_call, ...). A client-execution call is a valid TERMINAL output: the model emits the call and stops, waiting for the matching *_output, so no text accompanies it.
// A compaction-only reply (POST /v1/responses/compact, e.g. xAI) carries its state in a single compaction item.
hasContent = j.output.some(function (o) { return o && (o.type === 'message' || o.type === 'compaction' || /_call$/.test(o.type || '') || (o.content && o.content.length)); });
hasContent = j.embeddings.every(function (e) { return e && Array.isArray(e.values) && e.values.length > 0; });

// Nova answers with an array of {embedding, embeddingType} OBJECTS, where Bedrock Cohere answers with an array of bare vectors. Claimed before that branch, which matches on `embeddings` alone and would find no content in an array of objects - the failure that surfaced when folder 114 landed.
hasContent = j.embeddings.every(function (e) { return e && Array.isArray(e.embedding) && e.embedding.length > 0; });

} else if (Array.isArray(j.results) && j.results.length > 0 && j.results[0] && typeof j.results[0].index === 'number' && (typeof j.results[0].relevance_score === 'number' || typeof j.results[0].relevanceScore === 'number')) {

// A rerank response ranks the documents it was given; it generates no text, so the ranked list IS the content. Matched on index + a relevance score rather than on `results` alone, which is too generic to claim off other shapes. This branch went missing until now because no rerank row had ever returned 2xx: every bedrock row was rejected pre-flight for not naming its model as an ARN, and every vertex row 403s on discoveryengine IAM - and the content check is gated on code < 400, so it never ran.
} else if (Array.isArray(j.records) && j.records.length > 0 && j.records[0] && typeof j.records[0].id === 'string' && typeof j.records[0].score === 'number') {

// Discovery Engine's rank API is ID-keyed: it answers with records[] carrying id + score, not results[] with index + relevance_score, so the rerank branch above never claims it. Like that branch, the ranked list IS the content - a rank call generates no text. Matched on id + score rather than on `records` alone, which is too generic to claim off other shapes. This went missing because /genai/v1/rank only started returning the real Discovery Engine shape once the rank response converter landed; before that it leaked Bifrost's canonical results[] and was claimed by the rerank branch.
} else if (typeof j.url === 'string' && j.usage && j.extra_fields && j.extra_fields.request_type === 'speech') {
// A vendor that answers speech with a link to the audio (DashScope Qwen3-TTS, TXE-6433) is relayed as JSON carrying the link.
} else if (typeof j.name === 'string' && j.name.indexOf('/operations/') !== -1 && typeof j.done === 'boolean') {
// A GenAI video operation (generateVideos, or a poll of one). Until it is done the operation name IS the payload; a done one carries its videos as a uri or as videoBytes.
hasContent = !j.done || !!j.error || __samples.some(function (s) { var v = s && (s.video || s); return !!(v && (v.uri || v.videoBytes || v.bytesBase64Encoded || v.gcsUri)); });
// An async video job is a receipt, not content: submit returns {id, status} and
// the rendered asset only exists after polling. The id IS the payload.
} else if (typeof j.status === 'string' && typeof j.id === 'string' && (j.request_id || j.created_at)) {
// An async job is a receipt, not content: submit returns {id, status} and the result
// only exists once the job completes. The id IS the payload.
// POST /v1/mcp/tool/execute answers with one tool message; its content IS the result, a tool's own error text included.
hasContent = typeof j.content === 'string' ? j.content.length > 0 : Array.isArray(j.content) && j.content.length > 0;
// The /mcp server endpoint answers JSON-RPC: a result object is the payload, an error member is a failure.
pm.expect(hasContent, 'expected non-empty content (shape=' + shape + ', body=' + JSON.stringify(j).slice(0, 200) + ')').to.be.true;
// Routed-identity response headers (x-bifrost-*): present on every successful
// inference response, streaming and non-streaming, on native /v1 and every
// drop-in integration route, and passthrough (section 9) inference routes
// (all funnel through handleRequest, so RoutingInfo is populated).
// Management/list/file/batch/count ops are excluded by the positive path
// only when a fallback or key-alias fires) so they are not asserted here, and
// x-bifrost-routing-info-key is omitted (depends on operator key-naming).
// An async submission (/v1/async/...) answers 202 with a job, before any provider is called: it has no routed identity yet.
// An async submit (/v1/async/...) answers 202 with a job receipt before anything is routed, so
// it carries no routed identity; the job's result is read from GET /v1/async/.../{job_id}.
// Where the request was sent, not only that it was answered: a model carrying a provider prefix
// asks for that provider, and x-bifrost-routing-info-requested-provider must name it whatever
// routing rules, load balancing, sessions or fallbacks did afterwards. The model is read from the
// JSON or multipart body, or from the path on the Gemini-shaped routes, up to the last colon since
// a Bedrock id can contain one. Only standard provider names count as a prefix: a namespaced
// model such as meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B names no provider, and a custom provider is not known here.
if (__model === null && pm.request && pm.request.body && pm.request.body.mode === 'formdata' && pm.request.body.formdata) {
pm.test('Routed-identity header names the requested provider: ' + __prefix, function () {
// Streaming terminator contract for OpenAI-shaped completion streams (#7065).
// Bifrost writes a single `data: [DONE]` as the LAST frame of every successful
// /chat/completions and /completions SSE response, native and /openai drop-in,
// after any usage-only chunk (stream_options.include_usage) and after the
// post-hooks. A stream that ended on an error frame deliberately gets no marker,
// so the check stands down when a frame carries a top-level `error`.
// Responses, Anthropic, GenAI, Bedrock and image streams terminate differently
pm.test('SSE stream ends with a single [DONE] after any usage frame - #7065', function () {
pm.expect(__doneCount, 'expected exactly one [DONE] frame, got ' + __doneCount + ' across ' + __frames + ' frames').to.equal(1);
pm.expect(__afterDone, __afterDone + ' data frame(s) arrived after [DONE]; clients stop reading at the marker, so they are lost').to.equal(0);
pm.expect(__doneAt, 'usage frame at ' + __lastUsageAt + ' must precede [DONE] at ' + __doneAt).to.be.above(__lastUsageAt);
